title: AI Data Quality and Master Data Processes

questions.question: Why does master-data quality matter for AI workflows?
options: AI automatically fixes every source record before it reaches a downstream report
Data ownership stops mattering once a data-quality rule has been written down
AI can amplify duplicated, stale, undefined, or ownerless data problems
Sampling should always be avoided because it only checks a fraction of the records
questions.explanation: AI output quality depends on source-data quality and ownership — AI doesn't auto-fix bad records, ownership still matters even with a quality rule in place, and sampling (checking a fraction of records) is one of the lesson's recommended controls, not something to avoid.

questions.question: A customer master table has three separate rows for the same company, each with a slightly different name, and nobody has merged or flagged them. Which of the lesson's four signals does this match?
options: Missing owner — no one is accountable for approving or fixing changes to this table
Duplicate records — the same real-world entity is represented multiple times
Stale field — the values were correct once but haven't been refreshed recently
Definition gap — the team disagrees about what counts as an active customer
questions.explanation: Three rows for one company that were never merged is the lesson's duplicate-records signal — distinct from a missing owner (no accountable person), a stale field (an outdated single value), or a definition gap (disagreement about what a field means).

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A full data warehouse that replaces the team's existing operational database
A neural embedding model trained on the flagged duplicate and stale records
A final legal opinion on whether the data can be used for the AI use case
A ranked data-quality readiness plan with controls and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact is a triage tool that ranks scenarios into a data-quality readiness plan with controls and rationale — it doesn't build a warehouse, train an embedding model, or issue a legal opinion.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: Ignoring the data owner because the AI pipeline can proceed without accountability
Skipping the sample check since AI enrichment is assumed to catch bad records anyway
Hiding the definition gap so the backlog doesn't grow before the AI project ships
Quality rule — a testable, explicit definition of what a valid value looks like
questions.explanation: The lesson's controls are data owner, quality rule, sample check, and issue backlog — quality rule makes assumptions testable, unlike ignoring the owner, skipping sampling, or hiding a definition gap.

questions.question: When should a data issue become an AI readiness blocker?
options: Only when the underlying source data is already perfect and needs absolutely no further review — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
When ownership, duplicates, stale fields, or definitions stay unresolved for a high-impact use case
Only when there is no AI use case being considered for that data at all right now
Never — AI can reliably infer every missing data definition from context on its own
questions.explanation: High-impact AI use cases need resolved ownership, deduping, freshness, and definitions — not perfect data as a precondition, the absence of any AI use case, or blind trust that AI can infer definitions.

questions.question: What should teams create before scaling AI on operational data?
options: A single prompt template that works without referencing any source data at all, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
Named owners, testable quality rules, sample checks, and a data-quality backlog
An enrichment workflow that runs on operational data without any human review
A data definition that stays undocumented so the team can move faster
questions.explanation: The lesson's readiness controls are named owners, quality rules, sample checks, and a backlog for issues — not a prompt that ignores source data, an unreviewed enrichment workflow, or an undocumented definition.
